title: The integral residue coefficient complex is dualizable
statement: Fix a prime ℓ and a normed field E with a normed ℚ_ℓ-algebra structure. Use the continuous integral and residue coefficient objects and quotient map of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. For every scheme T, restrict the regular residue module on T along the integral quotient coefficient map and place it in degree zero of the derived category of internal integral module objects. This object is dualizable. No finite-dimensionality, finite-type, nonemptiness, or characteristic assumption on T is needed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), perfect coefficient input; the two-term free resolution of O_E/ℓ

proof.text: Apply exact monoidal inverse image from the profinite point to the proved integralModuleReductionSequence_shortExact. Exactness follows from left adjointness, preservation of finite limits, and additivity. Its first two terms are inverse images of the regular integral module.

Identify each of these terms with the regular module of the pulled integral ring. The isomorphism has the identity on underlying sheaves, and the action equation follows from monoidality. They are tensor units and hence dualizable.

Apply the proved library theorem DerivedCategory.isDualizable_singleFunctor_obj_of_shortExact to this short exact sequence and the two regular modules. Transport the third term through Functor.mapModComapIso and the inverse-image regular-module isomorphism. This is precisely the restricted residue module in the statement.

theorem integralResidue_isDualizable (T : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsDualizable ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      ((Mod.comap (coefficientMap (integralReductionMap ℓ E) T)).obj
        (Mod.regular (condensedRingObj
          (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} (integralResidue ℓ E)) T))))
